summary.headline: Satin Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 182% YoY to INR120 crore after absorbing a INR36 crore management overlay; reported ROA 3.55%.
summary.overview: Satin reported its 20th consecutive profitable quarter and its strongest Q1 in eight years, with consolidated AUM of INR15,935 crore (up 27% YoY, 5% QoQ) and record Q1 disbursements. Standalone NIM rose to 14.36% from 13.16% and cost-to-income improved to 44.49%. Management chose to absorb a INR36 crore management overlay, which lowered reported ROA to 3.55% (4.34% adjusted) and ROE to 15.10% (18.46% adjusted). Guidance for FY27 was kept at 20-25% consolidated AUM growth, 3-3.5% credit cost and 3.5-4% reported ROA, with a review at the half year.

financial_highlights.change: from 13.16% YoY; DA income INR94 crore in Q1 vs ~INR140 crore in Q4

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,360 crore, up 134% YoY and 29% QoQ across 121 branches in 14 states; CRAR 27.1%.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (SHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,263 crore, up 31% YoY; CRAR 59.8% across 57 branches in 22 states.

segments.name: Green finance book
segments.commentary: Reached INR624 crore; INR294 crore disbursed across 50 loans in Q1; ~45% of sustainable and emerging businesses portfolio in clean mobility and renewables.

segments.name: Satin Technologies / QTrino Labs
segments.commentary: First paying HRMS customers in Q1; QTrino Labs reached first customer revenue milestone. Core banking platform in customer UAT, go-live targeted Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives
segments.commentary: Progressing toward first close of Category 2 AIF, with first deployment expected in the coming quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated AUM growth of 20-25% in FY27, implying INR18,200-18,900 crore by March 2027.
Standalone reported credit cost of 3-3.5% for FY27, inclusive of any buffer built.
Standalone reported ROA of 3.5-4% for FY27; management expects QoQ ROA improvement from the 3.3% consolidated level.
NIM expected to stay in a 14.35-14.50% steady-state range.
Guidance to be reviewed at the half year depending on monsoon; long-term target INR32,000 crore consolidated AUM by 2030 with 30% from non-MFI.
Non-MFI share of consolidated AUM at 19% vs 14% a year ago; target 30% by 2030.
capex_capacity: Added 41 standalone branches in Q1; total 2,041 branches, 34 lakh clients, 3.9 lakh centres, 18,518 employees.
Commenced operations in Kerala in June 2026, adding to Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
392 branches added in FY26 are seasoning; operating expense ratio improved to 6.33% from 6.98% in Q4.
AUM per loan officer up 29% YoY.
Breakeven rule of thumb for a new branch: about 1,000 customers, typically reached in about 9 months.
INR100 crore promoter infusion approved by shareholders at about a 17% premium to the minimum issue price, to fund subsidiary growth.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter; management called Q1 disbursements the highest first-quarter disbursements in company history.

Assam floods hit 3 districts (Jorhat, Sivasagar, Charaideo): about 44,000 borrowers and INR149.83 crore outstanding affected, of which INR96.95 crore is covered by nat-cat insurance. Management says Assam ex-those districts is 100% on target.
Bank share of outstanding MFI loans fell to 26.4% from 32.6% a year ago; NBFC-MFI share rose to 43.7% from 38.9%.
Marginal cost of borrowing down 37 bps YoY to 10.52%; 77 active lenders; top 10 lenders are 52% of borrowing; INR2,000 crore direct assignment sanction from a public sector bank.
Undrawn sanctions of INR2,600 crore; INR3,000 crore raised in the quarter including INR285 crore subordinated debt (sub-debt total INR497 crore).

qa_highlights.question: How large should the management overlay buffer be built annually or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not committing to a number; the buffer depends on macro and field conditions and may not be needed. On-book provision is INR250 crore against an RBI requirement of INR152 crore.

qa_highlights.question: DA income trajectory and sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: DA is kept at 20-22% of AUM; Q1 DA was INR94 crore (Q4 was heavier at about INR140 crore). Q2 and Q3 should be in a similar range; Q4 is seasonally heavier.

qa_highlights.question: Gross slippages and write-offs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were INR49 crore (vs INR90 crore in Q4). Write-offs were INR127 crore, elevated because GNPA fell by about 90 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Stress from monsoon or Assam?
qa_highlights.answer: Assam is covered largely by nat-cat insurance; only about 5% of the Assam portfolio (INR149 crore) is affected, of which 3.5-4% is insured, leaving about 1% exposed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated AUM guidance lower than last quarter's 25-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says guidance is deliberately conservative; it expects to achieve 20-25% and stable-state growth of 20-25% in FY28 is not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is credit cost up while asset quality improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages halved to INR49 crore and GNPA fell 90 bps, but the overlay rose from a little over INR20 crore to INR36 crore, lifting reported credit cost.

risks_watch: Monsoon impact on rural cash flows over the next 2-3 months; Assam collections in the three flood-hit districts.
Negative carry from surplus liquidity: quarter-end drag about 0.15-0.20%, lower over the full quarter per management.
Forex: INR3 crore net negative impact in Q1 from hedged ECB (INR1,573 crore outstanding) accounting mismatch between servicing income and finance cost.
Subsidiary returns remain dilutive during scale-up; consolidated ROA is in an investment phase.
Credit cost guidance of 3-3.5% reported; further overlay additions would depress reported ROA.
key_quotes: We chose not to because we have just come through a cycle in which returns across the sector swung violently and we don't want to be among those who report their best numbers at the top and having nothing left when the turn comes.
So we are not committing a number to it. It will all depend on how the macroeconomics as well as the field level things pan out to be.

But what our idea is, we look at the complete ecosystem and the way how the field operations pan out to be, and that is the reason why we came out with this number and try and look at that and build that kind of a software.
But it's not a guidance. But having said that, we will probably be in the same bracket in the stable zone even in FY28.
Now 15.85% as compared to 14.50% is a slight aberration because the last quarter, as I always said, is probably the most heaviest quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and franchise durability, but deliberately cautious on returns: management chose to absorb a INR36 crore overlay and repeatedly framed guidance as conservative. Evasive on the size and cadence of future buffers, stating no number is committed, and on the FY28 growth outlook, which it called a stable-state view rather than guidance.

growth.why: FY27 consolidated AUM growth guided at 20-25% (INR18,200-18,900 cr by Mar-27), held; backed by 41 branches added in Q1 (2,041 total), Kerala launch, record Q1 disbursements (+56% consolidated) and a INR2,000 cr PSU bank assignment sanction, with INR2,600 cr undrawn sanctions, but no explicit capacity-to-growth bridge given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone NIM rose to 14.36% from 13.16% YoY and management guides a steady-state 14.35-14.50%, but DA income fell to INR94 crore in Q1 from ~INR140 crore in Q4 and surplus-liquidity negative carry (0.15-0.20% at quarter-end) is a drag, so further expansion is not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 41 standalone branches added in Q1 (total 2,041), Kerala commenced June 2026, and 392 FY26 branches are still seasoning; the brief gives no explicit capex figure, so this is branch rollout rather than a plant build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated disbursements up 56% YoY to INR3,495 crore, INR3,000 crore raised and INR2,600 crore undrawn sanctions plus a INR2,000 crore PSU bank assignment sanction support 20-25% AUM growth guidance (INR18,200-18,900 crore by March 2027) from INR15,935 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed and there is no utilisation figure; the business is branch-led and asset-light, with INR100 crore promoter infusion to fund subsidiary growth rather than a capex programme.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 AUM growth 20-25%, credit cost 3-3.5% and ROA 3.5-4% were all held, and the review is deferred to the half year depending on monsoon, with management stressing guidance is conservative but not signalling a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Overlay rose to INR36 crore (from ~INR20 crore) lifting reported credit cost to 3.06%, and any further overlay would push reported ROA below 3.5% against a 3.5-4% guide, with monsoon and Assam (about 1% of the portfolio exposed) as the watch items.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: QTrino Labs core banking platform is in customer UAT with go-live targeted Q2 FY27, and Category 2 AIF first deployment is expected in the coming quarter.

rows.label: Kerala launch and non-MFI diversification toward 30% by 2030
rows.why: Kerala operations commenced June 2026 and non-MFI share rose to 19% of consolidated AUM from 14% a year ago against a 30% target by 2030 (INR32,000 crore consolidated AUM).

rows.label: Assam flood exposure and nat-cat insurance cover
rows.why: INR149.83 crore outstanding in three flood-hit districts affecting ~44,000 borrowers, of which INR96.95 crore (about 65%) is covered by nat-cat insurance, leaving roughly 1% of the Assam portfolio exposed.

rows.label: Operating expense ratio improvement as FY26 branches season
rows.why: Operating expense ratio improved to 6.33% from 6.98% in Q4 and cost-to-income is 44.49%, with 392 FY26 branches seasoning and AUM per loan officer up 29% YoY.
